name: Constantine of Sicily
bio: Constantine of Sicily was a Byzantine grammarian and epigrammatist. His epigram on his professorial chair drew a sharp reply from Theophanes.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the fifth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XV: 13.

poems.title: Book XV, 13: On his Professorial Chair
poems.author: Constantine of Sicily
poems.text: If thou art one of the learned seat thyself on me, but if thou hast tasted of the Muse only with the tip of thy finger, .... stand at a distance from me and seek a seat elsewhere. I am a chair who supports men familiar with learning.
